title: About
text:
View my CV
Hi, I’m Emmanuel Dogbey, a WASH professional, spatial data analyst, and researcher based in Accra, Ghana, working at the intersection of WASH governance, geospatial analysis, and public policy. With a Master’s in Risk (Distinction) from Durham University and a First-Class BA in Geography and Rural Development from KNUST, I bring both academic rigour and practical experience to environmental health and sanitation systems strengthening.
Currently, I serve as Thematic Lead for Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) under the GoG–UNICEF Sanitation and Hygiene Programme, where I coordinate national efforts to co-develop and strengthen M&E frameworks, scale digital tools such as the Basic Sanitation Information System (BaSIS), design planning and budgeting tools with integrated Results-Based Financing (RBF) features, and contribute to the rollout of SMS-based monitoring systems. All of this supports and promotes evidence-based decision-making at national and sub-national levels.
I work across the full analytics pipeline—from data collection and cleaning to advanced analysis, spatial visualisation, and translation of insights to policy. My projects often combine statistical modelling, geospatial tools, and the production of decision-oriented reports and dashboards to support planning and programme management. For example, I have:

Modelled and predicted district-level waste collection rates using census data, district typologies, and regression analysis
Built an interactive R Shiny dashboard visualising status of sewage treatment facilities in Ghana
Developed an R-based workflow to query the Ghana Statistical Service’s StatsBank API, enabling reproducible access to official WASH indicators
Used Python to perform topic modelling and sentiment analysis on WASH and flood-related media content using NLP techniques.
Created custom mapping tools using Folium and Geopandas to overlay geocoded inputs on Ghana’s district boundaries

Beyond analytics, I contribute to broader systems strengthening, facilitating inter-agency coordination, supporting policy and strategy development, and embedding the use of data and place-based geospatial insights into national and district-level planning. I work closely with Government institutions, development partners, and civil society to promote alignment, uptake, and impact.
Over the years, I’ve contributed to national efforts on:

Climate-resilient WASH programming (supporting Ghana’s NDCs)
District sanitation monitoring and open defecation free validation
WASH financing using the Trackfin methodology
CLTS capacity building and community engagement
Environmental safeguards and solid waste management under the GARID Project

My technical toolbox includes R, Python, QGIS, ArcGIS, and the Microsoft Suite, with experience building tools, dashboards, and statistical models that support planning and policy. I’ve authored peer-reviewed publications on microplastic pollution, landfill siting, and wildfire risk, and regularly engage national and international partners to deliver high-impact, context-sensitive solutions.
I aim to bridge data and governance to help build and strengthen systems that are credible, actionable, and equitable.

title: Hi! I’m Emmanuel Dogbey
text:
I’m a WASH professional, data analyst, and researcher passionate about urban governance, environmental health, sanitation, wastewater, climate action, and public policy.
Welcome to my digital portfolio!
I build tools, models, and dashboards, and support the improvement and scale-up of national systems that help turn data into action. My work helps Government and partners strengthen planning, service delivery and monitoring across Ghana’s sanitation and hygiene sub-sector.
I also contribute to broader systems strengthening in the WASH sector by supporting policy and strategy development, coordinating across institutions as part of a wider whole-of-society approach for WASH governance, and embedding data use into national and district environmental sanitation governance through a place-based planning approach informed by geospatial analysis.

title: Featured Projects
text:
🧼 WASH Service Level Indicator Construction
Tools: R, dplyr, sf, purrr, janitor Overview: Cleaned and harmonized six national datasets (population, sanitation, waste, water access, etc.) to compute access indicators across 261 districts. Integrated spatial joins and regional metadata. Status: Delivered to CDD-Ghana for planning and advocacy. Deliverables: R script, Final dataset (CSV)

title: Featured Projects
section: ♻️ Predictive Modelling of Waste Collection Rates (2010–2021)
text:
♻️ Predictive Modelling of Waste Collection Rates (2010–2021)
Tools: R, ggplot2, lm, sf Overview: Built a linear regression model to estimate district-level solid waste collection rates from generation estimates and district types. Merged PHC datasets and visualized results using maps and residual plots. Status: Complete; ready for integration into dashboards or reports.

title: Featured Projects
text:
🌍 Sewage Facility Dashboard
Tools: R Shiny, leaflet, shinydashboard Overview: Interactive tool visualizing sewage treatment facilities across Ghana by region, condition, and type. Includes dynamic maps and summary tables. Status: MVP built; deployment pending. Source Code: GitHub Repository

title: Featured Projects
text:
🌐 StatsBank API Automation
Tools: R, httr2, jsonlite Overview: Created a full workflow for querying Ghana Statistical Service’s StatsBank API. Handled JSON logic, error handling, and data extraction for key WASH indicators from PHC 2021. Status: Script and tutorial complete; under version control. Tutorial: Blogpost-style HTML

title: Featured Projects
text:
🧪 Solid Waste Trends Visualization
Tools: R, ggplot2, sf Overview: Harmonized census waste data across 2010 and 2021, accounted for boundary changes, and visualized trends using choropleths and histograms. Highlighted disparities and temporal patterns. Status: Pipeline complete; supports planning insights.

title: Featured Projects
section: 🧠 Topic Modelling of Flood News Coverage
text:
🧠 Topic Modelling of Flood News Coverage
Tools: Python, Gensim, NLTK, Google CSE API Overview: Scraped and processed flood-related news (2010–2022) from Ghanaian sources. Applied LDA topic modelling and tuned using coherence scores to identify dominant reporting themes. Status: Topics finalized; visualization with pyLDAvis underway.

title: Featured Projects
section: 📰 Sentiment Analysis of Water Utility Coverage
text:
📰 Sentiment Analysis of Water Utility Coverage
Tools: Python, VADER, pandas Overview: Analyzed tone and emotional framing in post-2020 media coverage of the Ghana Water Company. Filtered low-information articles and generated outlet-wise sentiment summaries. Status: Preliminary results ready; dashboards in development.

title: Featured Projects
text:
🗺️ Geo-tagged Locator Map Tool
Tools: Python, Folium, Geopandas, Nominatim Overview: CLI-based tool that takes user input, returns geo-coordinates via Nominatim, and overlays location on Ghana district map using Folium. Status: Desktop-ready; web integration in progress.
